thread.title: Brewers Sweep Dodgers in NLCS, Reach First World Series Since 1982
thread.title_full: Brewers Sweep Dodgers in NLCS, Reach First World Series Since 1982

author: HeadTopics.com
title: Brewers Sweep Dodgers in NLCS, Reach First World Series Since 1982
text:
Milwaukee Brewers sweep Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS with a 6-4 win in Game 4, advancing to their first World Series since 1982.
The Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-4 in Game 4 of the National League Championship Series on Thursday, October 15, 2026, at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles, completing a sweep and advancing to their first World Series since 1982. The Dodgers, two-time defending champions, were eliminated after winning the title in 2024 against the New York Yankees and in 2025 against the Toronto Blue Jays.
Dodgers Take Early Lead Behind Ohtani
Los Angeles started Game 4 with a spark that had been missing all series. In the second inning, Andy Pages singled to center, and with two runners on, Shohei Ohtani crushed a three-run home run to center field, giving the Dodgers a 4-0 lead. It was Ohtani's first home run in his last 116 plate appearances, and manager Dave Roberts had moved him back to the leadoff spot after batting him sixth on Wednesday due to his slump.
Milwaukee used a bullpen game, with left-hander Shane Drohan opening and allowing one earned run in one inning. Former Dodger Dustin May then worked three innings, yielding three earned runs, all on Ohtani's homer. Right-hander Tyler Glasnow, who battled back problems all season, pitched 4.1 innings, giving up three hits and four runs while striking out six.
Brewers Rally and Seize Control
The Brewers began chipping away in the fourth. Glasnow issued a walk and allowed a double to William Contreras, followed by an RBI double from Jake Bauers to cut the deficit to 4-2. In the fifth, Sal Frelick walked and stole second, then David Hamilton singled to center to make it 4-3. Reliever Evan Phillips entered but allowed a hit and two walks, one intentional. Alex Vesia came in and walked in the tying run with the bases loaded, knotting the game at 4-4.
In the sixth, Garrett Mitchell homered to center to put Milwaukee ahead 5-4, a lead that felt decisive for a deflated Dodgers team. Los Angeles squandered chances to tie: in the seventh, Pages doubled and Kiké Hernández sacrificed him to third, but Ohtani struck out and Mookie Betts grounded out. They also left a runner on third in the eighth.
Hamilton's Clincher and World Series Berth
David Hamilton sealed the win with a solo home run off Edwin Díaz in the ninth, making it 6-4. Aaron Ashby recorded the final out for Milwaukee. The Brewers also avenged seven consecutive postseason losses to the Dodgers, including last year's NLCS sweep. Milwaukee now awaits the winner of the American League Championship Series.
Brewers manager Pat Murphy recalled a preseason prediction from Christian Yelich. Murphy said Yelich told the team they had better start believing because they were going to the World Series, and now they are here. Yelich added that it is a first big step and something they dreamed of as children, playing in a World Series, and that they trust themselves through good and bad times.
Murphy also praised Contreras, calling him a pitbull and joking that he only had about 20 minutes left because they were putting him in his corral, referencing Contreras's outstanding series. The Dodgers, with their high payroll and superstars, will now face an offseason of reflection after falling short against a Brewers team that proved baseball is not only about big salaries and star power.
